sense.text:
“In that day”: that is talking about the kingdom. “Will I assemble her that halteth”: halt means lame persons collectively, disabled, handicapped people who are crippled. This doesn’t mean that we are physically handicapped so much, but we are spiritually and mentally handicapped. We are all mentally and spiritually disabled, so we are the halt. We are the her that halteth, the disabled, and he is beginning now to assemble us.

“And I will gather her that is driven out”: the her that’s driven out is us. We’ve been driven out, scattered worldwide, and our goal, our mission, is to assemble the twelve tribes. That goal and that mission is too big to argue about on a street corner, too big to argue about a photograph.

“And her that I have afflicted”: God afflicted us. How? Slavery, oppression, colonialism. We’re the ones that God has afflicted.

“And I will make her that halted a remnant”: so we are the remnant. He’s not gathering all Israel, meaning he’s not gathering every Israelite on the planet. God is only gathering a remnant of the twelve tribes of Israel; a third will come up out of here and two-thirds are going to be put to death and die.

“And her that was cast far off a strong nation”: he’s going to make us into a strong nation. “And the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever”: the Lord is going to reign over that mighty remnant of Israel.

“And thou, O tower of the flock”: Jerusalem is the tower of the flock, “the strong hold of the daughter of Zion,” because Jerusalem is going to be the capital of the planet Earth, the capital of the world.

“Unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion”: that’s Christ. We’re going to have the greatest King, and he’s going to rule from sea to sea. It’s going to come as the dominion of Christ.

“The kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem”: so the kingdom ain’t coming to everybody. The kingdom is only for Jerusalem, the daughter of Jerusalem.

“Now why dost thou cry out aloud?” The Lord is asking us. We cry for our sons and daughters being murdered, day by day, week by week, month by month, year by year, slain in the streets. We get tired, we are hurt, we are crying. But there’s a divine purpose behind all these deaths, and it’s only going to escalate until we acknowledge our offense.

“Is there no king in thee?” Our people say we got no king but Caesar, meaning the white man. Until our people realize that there is only one king, the Lord and Savior whom the world calls Jesus Christ, we will always suffer here in this land and worldwide.

“For pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail”: the pains that take hold of us like a woman in travail are the constant oppression, the tribulation that’s coming, all the day by day incidents we see on the news. Like a woman in travail: when is it going to end? It ain’t going to end until Israel wakes up and repents, till that number is reached.

“Be in pain”: this is a message to the teachers. Yes, it’s going to hurt. We must do this job regardless of what we go through in our personal lives, whether we have lost sons or daughters, mothers or fathers; no matter what, we must continue and push. “And labour to bring forth” means to work: labor to bring forth the remnant of Israel. “O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”: we’re going to have pains here and pains there in this truth.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: we left the city of Jerusalem, “and thou shalt dwell in the field,” meaning the world, “and thou shalt go even to Babylon,” and we’ve gone even to Babylon the great; that’s this place right here.

“There shalt thou be delivered”: we were not delivered in ancient Babylon; Persia took over and conquered. This Babylon is Babylon the great, the United States of America. “There the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies”: so the Lord ain’t redeeming all races, all people; he’s only redeeming the Israelites. From what? Their enemies. Some of our people don’t even believe they got enemies, it’s all love. It’s not all love: we have enemies who plot from sun up to sun down.

“Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled”: let the Israelites be defiled. “And let our eye look upon Zion”: we are Zion. So the nations have gathered themselves against us.

“But they know not the thoughts of the Lord”: these nations who have looked upon us for evil, who have destroyed our people, who have consistently set up a political system of oppression nonstop, some we see and some we don’t, what they call systematic racism. The nations don’t know the thoughts of the Lord, with all their stupid religions. “Neither understand they his counsel”: his counsel is the Bible; these nations do not understand the Bible. “For he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.”

“Arise and thresh”: this is what the Lord is saying to us. Thresh means to separate grain from a plant, and it is a variant spelling of thrash: to beat a person or animal repeatedly and violently with a stick or whip, to hit something hard and repeatedly, to move in a violent and convulsive way. God is telling the Israelites to rise up and beat the hell out of the nations. Arise, wake up Israel. “O daughter of Zion”: we the daughter of Zion.

“For I will make thine horn iron”: he’s going to give us power. “And thou shalt beat in pieces many people”: we going to beat in pieces many people. I don’t know what Bible the Christians are reading.

“And I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord”: their gain is the forces of the Gentiles, their wealth, brought into Jerusalem. “And their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth”: that’s Christ, of that first dominion you read about in verse 8.

precepts.why: To be driven out: James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad.” That scattered abroad means driven out. We’ve been driven out, scattered worldwide, and our goal, our mission, is to assemble the twelve tribes. Everyone needs to understand that.

How God afflicted us. “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up”: the nations eat up all our labors, all our work, all our resources. Everything we put our hand to the plow for, they reap the benefits. It goes with what was said about Lazarus, how the dogs would come and lick his wounds.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”: that’s the part right there. That is our life. We’re the ones that God has afflicted, from slavery, oppression, colonialism.

God is only gathering a remnant. “In all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: two-thirds of us will die in this land here, “but the third shall be left therein.”

“And I will bring the third part through the fire”: that is twofold, spiritual and literal. “And will refine them as silver is refined”: in a spiritual sense we’re being refined right now when he teaches us his laws, by keeping the commandments. We have our ups and downs, ins and outs, our trials and shortcomings, but we rise and get back up.

Literally, when we come through the fire he refines us; that’s him pleading with us face to face, and he’s going to teach us the laws, and it’s do or die on that day. It ain’t no ‘oh I committed adultery today, I’m sorry, forgive me.’ Nope, you dead. Rehearsal time is up, it’s over, it’s finished. That’s when he brings us under the bond of the covenant you read about in Ezekiel chapter 20. Right now we’re under the New Covenant, called grace.

About that first dominion: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” Christ shall have dominion. That’s the first dominion, the great dominion, the dominion of Christ that comes to the tower of the flock, Jerusalem.

This is why the apostles asked this question that the churches ignore: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The kingdom is only for Israel. They asked, is this the time, Lord? And Christ said the time is not for you to know yet.

So the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem, and the kingdom ain’t for all nations, the kingdom ain’t for all races. The kingdom’s only for the Israelites.

There is a divine purpose behind all these deaths. Parents will ask, why Lord, why is this happening? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence”: our people refuse to acknowledge that as the Israelites we have sinned.

“And seek my face”: our people refuse to seek God’s face as the Israelites. To seek his face means you got to open his Bible and read the Bible with Israelite eyes and see yourself. You are the people of the book, but our people don’t want to do that.

“In their affliction they will seek me early.” That’s why there’s a reason behind all these deaths, and it’s only going to escalate.

Some of you think online the Democrats will save us; some of you think the Republicans will save us. Sad and bad news for all of you: none of them can save us. The deaths of our sons and daughters will only escalate until we acknowledge our offense; that’s what the Bible says.

“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” Every generation there’s a new group of negroes who got a bright idea: let’s be Democrats, or let’s be Republicans, or let’s be conservatives, let’s be something in the system. Somebody tell the Christians: the white man can’t save us. His political parties can’t save us. His false religions can’t save us. The Bible prophesies it: we have watched for a nation that could not save us.

Be in pain: no matter what we lose, we must continue and push, because we believe this. “Thy brother shall rise again”: your brother, your loved one, shall rise again. Martha said, “I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

“I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.” Whosoever liveth and believeth in him means you keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ.

“Believest thou this?” That is the question we all have to answer: do you believe that?

Labor to bring forth the remnant of Israel. “Give diligence to make your calling and election sure.” Why give diligence? “For if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”: if you give diligence in God’s work, you shall never fall. We got to believe that thing.

“But watch thou in all things”: don’t just watch the news; watch in your own home, watch in your local congregations, watch what’s going on. “Endure afflictions”: endure whatever comes your way; we all must endure afflictions.

“Do the work of an evangelist”: don’t just sit home on your computer. If you sick and ailing we understand that, but if you are strong and able bodied, the Bible says you men do the work of an evangelist. Five brothers here don’t have a driver’s license. There may be reasons, child support or whatever, but don’t be a lazy brother. On one of our first trips we drove to Canada and took turns driving, and the black ninja sat in the back seat eating Kentucky Fried Chicken. When it was his turn to drive: I don’t know how to drive. Thirty-five years old with no driver’s license, simple as hell. On a simple mission to drive to Canada he just sat there going and coming eating chicken. That’s a useless brother; you’re useless.

That’s the basic driver’s license; from there, the passport. If you can’t travel on a plane, you can at least get in a cab, or get on the train and go locally and be a local prophet; there’s no shame in that, stay right there in your little community. But if you want to go where no man has gone before, do the work of an evangelist.

“Make full proof of thy ministry”: you have to make full proof of your ministry. Just having fringes on is not making full proof of your ministry. That’s not about the brother who is sick or handicapped; the Lord got them, that’s a special breed, they do what they can. It’s about able brothers who just sit around and scratch and eat chicken and watch porn. That’s who this is talking to.

This all covers be in pain, and labor, and labor, and labor to bring forth. “And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity”: because we going to be afflicted here, we going to catch hell. “And the water of affliction”: we cry at the things we see and the things we go through. That’s the water of affliction: our tears, our wives’ tears, our sons’ and daughters’ tears.

“Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more”: why? Because your teachers will make full proof of their ministry; they will go where no man has gone before. “But thine eyes shall see thy teachers”: you going to see the men and say these are the men of God, these are the only men that’s taking that Bible serious.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee”: behind thee, because some of our people are walking in the wrong direction, walking away from this truth. “Saying, This is the way, walk ye in it”: brothers and sisters, this is the way. “When ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left”: when you turn to the right hand you’re going to hear this truth, and when you turn to the left you’re going to hear this truth, because this truth will cover this earth.

“I will make thine horn iron”: he’s going to give us power. “Until the Ancient of days came”: until the time that God came, “and judgment was given to the saints of the most High.” The judgment that’s given to us is power. Right now we weak as hell; we can’t come against China, we can’t even come against the ones on the corner. The Lord said I got to give you power; judgment must be given to you.

“And the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom”: that’s the judgment. The time came that the saints possessed this planet Earth.

“Thou shalt beat in pieces many people”: that’s what Christ said. So what Bible is Jamal Bryant reading, what Bible are the Seventh Day Adventists and the Christians reading?

“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works”: to keep Christ’s works means keep his commandments, “unto the end.” We got to keep them works unto the end. “To him will I give power over the nations.” It’s a hard thing for blacks and Latinos to comprehend, because we ain’t never had nothing, we ain’t never been nothing; we can’t conceive that we are God’s special and anointed people.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: we going to rule the nations with a rod of iron; we ain’t going to play with them. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: that’s that thresh we just read in Micah 4. “Even as I received of my Father”: the same rulership Christ got, he said I’m going to give it to you, because according to Romans 8 we are joint heirs with Christ.

“I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord.” “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night”: the gates of Jerusalem shall be opened continually, morning or evening time, “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles.” That’s the gain consecrated from the nations: the forces of the Gentiles is their wealth. “And that their kings may be brought”: we going to bring their kings too.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: any rebellious kingdom out there. “Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

sense.text:
“Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops”: the Lord is saying, gather yourselves together. Out of all the nations he spoke of in Micah 4, now he turns to Rome. It was prophecy back then; now we look back on it and it is history.

“He hath laid siege against us”: that is what Rome did when it came against us.

“They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek”: the they is this white man, the they is Rome. Rome smote the judge of Israel, Christ, with a rod upon the cheek, and mocked him.

precepts.why:
The laying of siege against us in Micah 5:1 is what Moses foretold. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth.” Just as Greece’s symbol was the eagle, so was Rome’s symbol the eagle, so this is read in the context of Rome. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: Rome spoke Latin. “A nation of fierce countenance”: Rome was a nation of fierce countenance, which would “not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young.” They didn’t care if we were old Israelites or young Israelites.

“He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”: Rome took over everything. They even forced us to pay taxes, and all those laws of taxation America has today they got from back there with Rome.

“And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates”: the same thing as Micah 5:1, “he hath laid siege against us.” “Until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst”: they tore down the walls of Jerusalem, and we had trusted that Rome could never defeat us because of those walls. It was a seven-year siege. There were three wars, but the main one was under Titus in the year 70.

“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters”: Rome did not allow any food in and cut off the water system. They starved us out; they didn’t even have to lift a sword against us. They said, cut everything off, give it time, they’ll die or come begging for food, and we resorted to cannibalism. It is the same here in America the way the system is set up: the trucks come in and out of our cities, and all America has to do is cut off the trucks. It happened in Canada with the trucking incident, when the truckers revolted and they shut the trucks down and shut down the bank accounts.

“The man that is tender among you, and very delicate” is not talking about a homo; it is a prince, a leader, a princely man. “His eye shall be evil toward his brother, and toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the remnant of his children”, “so that he will not give to any of them of the flesh of his children whom he shall eat: because he hath nothing left him in the siege.” “The tender and delicate woman among you, which would not adventure to set the sole of her foot upon the ground” is a princess, one who has servants; “she shall eat them for want of all things secretly in the siege”: she too resorted to cannibalism.

Brothers use verses 54 to 57 for today, for the evil our people are doing now. That is fine, but understand the proper context and explain it first: this is talking about the siege. Then bring that part out for what is going on today, so you don’t get caught out on the street and end up in a video about you being a dumbass.

Everybody likes to say I’m free, I’m independent, I’m an entrepreneur. Watch what Nehemiah says: “Behold, we are servants this day, and for the land that thou gavest unto our fathers to eat the fruit thereof and the good thereof, behold, we are servants in it.” Servants in our own land.

“And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”: in the time of Nehemiah God had set the Persian kings over us. “Also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” We don’t like to admit it, but the Bible says these nations, these kings, have dominion over our bodies.

Imagine that: we are a nation here in exile, and our food and water depend on our enemies. You free, you independent, you entrepreneurs, the hell you are: you are servants this day. If this white man cuts off the ins and outs of the ships and the trucks, we are finished here. That is why we must depend on the one true God, and why the siege of Deuteronomy 28 speaks to us still.

This goes with “they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.” “And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him. And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face”: they blindfolded Christ, that is what Rome did, and struck him on the face. They “asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?” They were mocking the Lord, “and many other things blasphemously spake they against him.”

“Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him”: they beat Jesus. “The soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe, and said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.” They put a purple robe on Christ and started punching him in the face, smacking him upside the head: the judge of Israel smitten upon the cheek.

“The soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers. And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.” “When they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!”

That spirit right there is still in white America. When you tell them Christ is black they make a mockery of it; many of them say they will never serve a black God, a black king. That is the same thing Rome was doing here.

“And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head”: they hit him upside the head, the smiting of Micah 5:1.

Christ said it himself through the prophet: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair.” He gave his cheeks: they were ripping the hair off his face. “I hid not my face from shame and spitting”: he didn’t hide his face from shame and spitting. We really don’t know what the Lord went through for us.

sense.text:
“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel”: Micah is telling you that God would send his son for us. The ruler that comes out of Bethlehem Ephratah is Christ; he is the King of kings and Lord of lords.

“Whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting”: Christ is the one who has been from of old, from everlasting. He was prophesied way back then.

precepts.why: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” See that: “that shall rule my people Israel.” The ruler in Israel that Micah said would come forth out of Bethlehem is the Governor Matthew names, Christ, born in Bethlehem.

sense.text:
“Therefore will he give them up”: that means captivity. The Lord gave us up, smote us and scattered us for idolatry.

“Until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth”: brought forth what? Believers. He gave us up into captivity until the time believers came forth, awake to righteousness, bringing forth fruit.

precepts.why:
He gave us up. “For the Lord shall smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and he shall root up Israel out of this good land, which he gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the river.” He smote us and scattered us beyond the river.

“Because they have made their groves, provoking the Lord to anger”: in those groves we were worshipping false gods. “And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.” The sin of Jeroboam was idolatry, the same thing we are doing today. So we got smitten by the Lord and scattered for idolatry: that is the giving up of Micah 5:3.

“Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth”: what she brings forth is believers who “Awake to righteousness, and sin not.” The giving up lasts until our people wake up to Christ and keep the commandments.

sense.text:
“Awake to righteousness, and sin not”: awake to Christ, keeping the commandments. Ask a Christian and he’ll say that righteousness just means Jesus. It would be nice if that were all it meant, but in Christianity they have been taught by the pope to separate God’s laws from the faith in Christ. Christ is the righteousness in keeping the commandments, because that is how you show your faith: you say you believe in the Lord, then show us your works, for faith without works is dead.

“For some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.” Then a true story that just came out. We set brothers up with sisters to learn each other, and send them out with a chaperone, so there is no hanky panky, no nitty-gritty, because we know some of y’all are nasty. A brother said he wanted to prove a sister for one to two years. A husband and wife were sent to chaperone. At dinner the husband chaperone was playing toes with the sister he was supposed to be chaperoning. The brother proving her, simple as hell, said he would stop talking to her at 9:00 p.m. so as not to abuse her; at 9:01 she was calling the husband: meet me at the telly. The husband was banging the girl he was supposed to chaperone, and his pregnant wife, who was chaperoning too, didn’t know. When she had the baby, sister ho offered to come help with the delivery as a midwife. See how wicked this thing is, you evil black men and nasty black women out there.

So read the verse again, and if you get mad, suck it up, dry your eyes: “Awake to righteousness, and sin not.” God says when you wake up in this truth, stop the blood clot sinning.

Brothers, don’t believe women when they cry; tears don’t work on me. When she was confronted she was asking what did I do wrong, I didn’t do nothing wrong, huffing and puffing with the snot bubbles coming out the nose, and it got so bad she said maybe she got raped. Stop the lies. You’re supposed to be able to trust brothers in this truth, and here the older brother you trusted to chaperone is banging her behind the scenes.

Just as Paul spoke this to the shame of the Corinthians, we bring this out to our shame here in IUIC. We never said we are perfect. We have broken soldiers here, broken men and broken women, and we are trying to fix them. Some brothers and sisters take the healing and get healed; some refuse the medicine and refuse to be fixed.

precepts.why: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” See that: the commandments and the faith, together. The righteousness we awake to is not faith in Jesus with God’s laws cut off from it; the saints keep both.

Watch what Christians do; these damn Christians get on my nerves. They take “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth” and put it with “Awake to righteousness” and say, see, don’t do the law.

But the law there is the law of sacrifice, because that is how we got forgiven. Christ did away with the law of animal sacrifice and fulfilled that law by his own sacrifice. He is not the end of the commandments: Christ is the righteousness in keeping the commandments, because that is how you show your faith.

sense.text:
“Therefore will he give them up”: he gave us up into captivity. “Until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth”: now we are bringing forth fruits of righteousness. We have woken up to the truth that we are the Israelites, and we are doing our best, to the best of our ability, to bring forth fruits of righteousness.

“Then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel”: we are returning as the children of Israel, returning to the truth that we are the children of Israel. We are leaving from being African American to the children of Israel; leaving from being Jamaican and Puerto Rican and Mexican to the children of Israel.

precepts.why:
“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Then: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.” The great and dreadful day of the Lord is the second coming of Christ, and before it he prophesied he would send Elijah.

“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers”: that is what we just read in Micah 5:3, “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” When Elijah came he was returning us to our fathers. The fathers are Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the prophets; we are the children.

“Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse”: the Lord said if I don’t do that, I will have to destroy the planet.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”: it is being said that we are not God’s people by these Gentile names put on us, all these Gentile labels the white man has put on us.

“There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” That started with Elijah coming back: you’re not African American, you’re not Puerto Rican, you’re not Mexican, you are the Israelites, you are the sons of the living God. Elijah started it, and we are following suit and continuing on.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together”: the gathering is not all races on the planet. It is the children of Judah and the children of Israel, the two kingdoms coming together, and they “appoint themselves one head”, one king, that first dominion.

“And they shall come up out of the land”: what the church calls the rapture is that great day of deliverance, when Judah and Israel come up out of the land, “for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” Everybody isn’t coming up out of this land when destruction comes; it is only Judah and Israel. That is the remnant returning unto the children of Israel.

sense.text:
“And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God”: the majesty, that is Christ.

“And they shall abide: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth”: Christ is going to be great unto the ends of the earth, of the world. Look at that power: we don’t see ourselves like nothing, but that is our King, and the Lord is going to be powerful.

precepts.why:
“And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”: he is going to cut off wars. “And he shall speak peace unto the heathen”: we are the heathen; the Israelites are the ones called the heathen.

“And his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth”: Christ’s dominion. The heathen get mad; the Palestinians have that slogan ‘from the river to the sea.’ Well, we are going to use this one: “from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” That is how great he shall be unto the ends of the earth.

Somebody is going to say, we’re not heathens. Oh yes we are: as long as we are African American, Puerto Rican, Haitian, those are heathen names.

sense.text:
“And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”: he’s going to cut off wars.

“And he shall speak peace unto the heathen.” We the heathen. Christ is going to speak peace to the heathen, and the heathen he speaks peace to is the Israelites; we are the ones called the heathen. Somebody right now is going, we’re not heathens. Oh yes we are. As long as we are African American, Puerto Rican, Haitian, those are heathen names.

“And his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” That is Christ’s dominion. Don’t the heathen get mad with that slogan the Palestinians got, ‘from the river to the sea’? They mad. Well, we going to use this one: from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.

precepts.why: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. See that: the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen. Our own enemies say it of us.

“And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.”

So our people in these religions, false religions, serving wood and stone, are as the heathen. That is why the Lord said he’s going to speak peace to the heathen: that’s us.

This goes back to the peace, speaking peace to them. “I Esdras received a charge of the Lord upon the mount Oreb, that I should go unto Israel”; go unto Israel. “But when I came unto them, they set me at nought, and despised the commandment of the Lord.”

So because of that, watch: “And therefore I say unto you, O ye heathen”. Who? O ye heathen. He’s talking to Israel. “That hear and understand, look for your Shepherd”: that’s the Shepherd in Micah 5.

“He shall give you everlasting rest”: that’s speaking peace to us, the same thing. “For he is nigh at hand, that shall come in the end of the world.” That was a heavy one.

Canary Mission: they got IUIC in there, they got the Bishop all up in there, and they put your picture there to put you in fear and get you terminated from your job. That’s Amalek. An article on the ADL partnering with J. Edgar Hoover’s COINTELPRO to destroy black leaders and organizations shows it. The charge of anti-Semitism has been weaponized to make all who are smeared with it a pariah in the eyes of the public. That’s what all those groups do: they smear your name, call you an anti-Semitic group, and it’ll get you terminated. They’ve gotten a lot of people kicked out of universities and colleges. They a real hate group. Reading that article about Farrakhan does not mean we Muslim, and we are not joined hand in hand with no group.

The ADL is an extension of J. Edgar Hoover’s COINTELPRO: all FBI regional offices were instructed to work with them. That’s how you know Amalek is all in society. They the devil. “Then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men.” Seven and eight is fifteen.

precepts.why:
“The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”.

So he ain’t preaching peace to all the people on the planet. He’s preaching peace to the Israelites. This man, the peace of Micah 5:5, is Christ.
“Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ”. See that: we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. He is the peace.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. He made both kingdoms into one, one nation.

“And hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”. The wall he broke down that stood between us was the law of sacrifice; that’s the wall of partition that was between us.

“And came and preached peace to you which were afar off”: that’s our people scattered across the planet. And to them that were nigh: those were the ones in Jerusalem. Christ preached peace to both, because he is the peace.

We’re still dealing with the peace: Christ is our peace. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: ‘for God so loved the world he gave his only begotten son.’

“And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: Christ is establishing a government. Believe it or not, what you see at IUIC is just the beginning stages; the government is shaping and forming.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God”: Christ is the mighty God. “The everlasting Father”: Christians, and even Israelites, can’t explain that Christ is the everlasting Father. They think the Most High in the Old Testament was the father. No, that’s Christ. Christ is the everlasting Father that we dealt with from the time of Moses. Some Israelite camps is mad, they cursed the Bishop out and said he’s a heretic; but it tells you right there, Christ is the everlasting Father.

And here’s the part we want: “The Prince of Peace.” Christ is our Prince of Peace, and that is the man who shall be the peace in Micah 5:5.

This is what Christians do with the Assyrian coming into our land. A Christian pastor in Texas named John Hagee uses this verse: “Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children.”

They use that verse to say that’s the fulfillment of May 14th, 1948. What we read in Isaiah 66 ain’t talking about May 14th, 1948. You Michelin man, you better cut it out with your lies. They don’t want us on TV with these guys.

That’s what Canary Mission is, and Amalek treading in our palaces. “For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death”: the morning means the word of God, the light of God. It is unto them even as the shadow of death.

“If one know them”, if you know the light of God, “they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.” So Canary Mission and the rest are so fearful that this truth goes out that what they try to do is destroy your job, your career. It’s all Amalek.

This is the precept for the seven shepherds and eight principal men. Seven and eight is fifteen brothers. “Behold what glory”: “Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Oseas, Amos, and Micheas, Joel, Abdias, and Jonas, Nahum, and Abacuc, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zachary, and Malachy, which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

Oseas is Hosea. Micheas is Micah, that we’re reading about now. Abdias is Obadiah. Abacuc is Habakkuk. Sophonias is Zephaniah. Aggeus is Haggai. Zachary is Zechariah, and Malachy is Malachi. That’s fifteen. So those seven shepherds and eight principal men are listed right there: the leaders the Lord is raising up against the Assyrian.

But guess what, there’s more. That ain’t all the Lord got. “For thy help will I send my servants”: the first is Isaiah, and Jeremy, that’s Jeremiah, “after whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits”. Those twelve trees are the twelve apostles.

This next part is just a thought, no scripture: it once seemed that Abraham was one of the twelve. But then remember, Christ said Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and he saw it, and the Pharisees couldn’t understand that: you ain’t fifty years old. Christ spoke some levels in there, and that is for another time.

sense.text:
“And they shall waste the land of Assyria”: the land of Assyria is modern day Israel. “With the sword”: nobody is running over there with a literal sword. The sword is the word of God.

So when you read the Bible, when you read Revelation 2:9, Revelation 3:9, Ezekiel 7:14, you are laying waste with the sword the land of Assyria, which is modern Israel, because they feel the spiritual repercussions. This is why their groups, the ADL, the SPLC, the Simon Wiesenthal Center, Canary Mission and AIPAC, have a vendetta: we got to stop these guys. They tell YouTube to shadow ban us, slow down our videos, don’t let them reach this country or that country. They don’t cover us in the news: thousands of us in California, the helicopter circling us, and no news footage.

See what they did to Kyrie Irving and Ye. A little small thing, a post, and they said destroy them. Any ball player that tweeted anything favorable to us, they went after him. Nick Cannon, Kyrie Irving, they were all re-educated: they had to give money to the ADL and get brainwashed again. It’s like a freaking Matrix we’re in. People ask why they went so hard at Kyrie, it’s just a post. It’s not just a post. This is war in the spirit world.

“And the land of Nimrod”: the land of Nimrod is Babylon, and that is this place right here, America. So we are hitting them on two fronts with the Bible, the word of God: we’re getting them over there and we’re getting them over here.

“Thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.” This is letting us know that Amalek is going to attack us. You think we are going to prophesy the counsel of the Lord and this Assyrian, these Amalekites, ain’t going to respond?

precepts.why:
You may see “with the sword” and think, wait a minute, ain’t nobody running over there with no literal sword. Here is what it is talking about: “For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

So that’s the sword. The sword that wastes the land of Assyria is the word of God, and every time the Bible is read and taught, that sword is cutting.

Here is how the land of Assyria and the land of Nimrod get wasted: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.”

The righteous, the ones they afflicted and made no account of, stand up in boldness before their face with the word of God. That is the sword going forth.

“And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of his mouth is the Bible. We are consuming them with the spirit of God’s mouth, the Bible.

“And shall destroy with the brightness of his coming”: the Lord is going to destroy them with the brightness of his coming. The word wastes them now, and Christ finishes them when he comes.

“And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt”: the land of Judah is talking about those men he is raising up, the seven shepherds and eight principal men, and they shall be a terror unto Egypt. This Egypt is spiritual Egypt, which is America. “Every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself”: be afraid, be very afraid.

But see why: “because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts.” Not because of us. Because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, and that means because of the Bible. People hear it and say, wait, that’s the Bible you’re reading? We never heard that before. It is the counsel “which he hath determined against it”, against Egypt.

Verse 18: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan”: a lot of cities here in America. The language of Canaan goes back to verse 17, the counsel of the Lord of hosts. That is the language of Canaan. “And swear to the Lord of hosts” means we dedicate ourselves to the Lord of hosts.

“One shall be called, The city of destruction.” There are going to be a lot of prophecies coming out of a particular city, and it is going to lay waste, spiritual waste and devastation, to this place, because the Lord is going to be answering those prayers. His angels are going to be getting activated as the word of God goes out from there.

You think we can prophesy the counsel of the Lord and the Assyrian won’t respond? “And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman.” Put the ADL back up there, all them little groups they got: this is the serpent. The mouth of the serpent is their media. The water is all their lies and deceptions. The American Empire’s media is controlled by Amalek; they control all this media.

They can block us all they want; we got boots on the ground, and we’ll go to that underground railroad if we have to. The mouth of the serpent, the media, is what they are going to use to slander us, to call us a hate group, to call us violent, to call us terrorists, and turn the whole world against us in the future. That is the red dragon.

“That he might cause her to be carried away of the flood. And the earth helped the woman”: the earth that helped the woman is the word of God. “And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood which the dragon cast out of his mouth.” The only thing that can swallow up every lie is the Holy Bible. That’s why we got to learn our book; we got to learn the counsel of the Lord.

“And the dragon was wroth with the woman”: the dragon was pissed off with the Israelites. “And went to make war with the remnant of her seed.” This is war, and this war is physical. Right now they shadow ban the brothers and don’t put them on the news, but that war right there ain’t spiritual. They are going to arrest, kill, lame, destroy, take homes, take houses, take property. That’s what the Bible is saying they are going to do.

“Which keep the commandments of God”: they are afraid of the commandments of God, because that is where the power is. “And have the testimony of Jesus Christ”: and we got the testimony of Jesus Christ.

This is what the Assyrian is going to do when he comes into our land. This is what the ungodly is going to do; this is what the white man is going to do. “Let us oppress the poor righteous man, let us not spare the widow”: they don’t care if a woman’s husband is dead, to hell with her. “Nor reverence the ancient gray hairs of the aged”: they don’t care how old the Negro is, to hell with him, just like ancient Rome.

“Let our strength be the law of justice.” Who’s training the FBI? The ADL. They are the ones making legislation. AIPAC is giving each candidate millions and millions of dollars, so that whoever wins puts in place their agendas. There are no accidents going on. It don’t matter if Kamala Harris wins or Trump, the damn devil, wins. They also became presidents in places down in Mexico and South America. That’s all strategic, that’s all chess: they are moving themselves into positions of power to mobilize, because as we travel and spread the word of God they are going to keep an eye on us in all these regions.

“Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn”: he ain’t supporting us, he’s not for the Talmud. “And he is clean contrary to our doings”: opposite to their doings. “He upbraideth us with our offending the law”: they claim to be Jews and Christians, and we are proving you are not Jews, you are not Christians, you don’t keep nothing the Torah says. “And objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education”: their education is the Talmud. They are not educated in the Torah or the Tanakh; the Torah is the first five books of Moses and the Tanakh is Genesis to Malachi. They don’t follow the instructions in that; they follow the Talmud and the Kabbalah.

“He professeth to have the knowledge of God”: we’re the ones professing to have the knowledge of God. “And he calleth himself the child of the Lord”: we are the children of God, like Hosea 1:10 said. “He was made to reprove our thoughts. He is grievous unto us even to behold”: they despise the way we look. That’s why they changed Black Jesus to a white Jesus, and that’s why they changed the black Jews to white Jews.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: another word for counterfeits is fakes, phonies. It is saying Revelation 2:9 and Revelation 3:9, the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. “He pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”: we are telling the world, no matter what happens, we are going to rule this planet under Christ, the 12 tribes. “And maketh his boast that God is his father”: God is our father and nobody else’s.

“Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him. For if the just man be the son of God, he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.” They are mocking us, the same as they did to Christ on the cross, when they mocked him and said, if he is the Son of God, let him come down.

“Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.” Don’t just run by that: this is what they want to get to. It is the same thing Christ warned us about in Matthew 24, where they’ll take you into the synagogues and beat you and scourge you and imprison you and kill you. Let us see if he believes that; let’s see if he’s going to confess Christ to the point of death, or give up Christ.

This is why they look for our people that start to wake up in different lands and send groups out there to convert them with a little stupid hat. When we were in Papua New Guinea a brother walked over to us with a little stupid hat and a little dirty prayer shawl. That ain’t in the Bible; show it to me if you say it is. The church out there was being sent a couple of G’s a month, so they said, we have an allegiance with Israel. If you want salvation, to hell with their money.

Torture is not a regular death. Torture means they might take away your fingernails, cut off one of your fingers, cut one of your ears: they are going to dismantle your body before they put you to death. “Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected. Such things they did imagine, and were deceived: for their own wickedness hath blinded them. As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not”: they don’t know them. “Neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness, nor discerned a reward for blameless souls.”

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly.” We fast now, but this is talking about a day that is going to come when we are going to have to call a major global fast. “Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders”: this is why your congregations need elders. You cannot have a congregation with children running it; you need an elder, somebody from old time that’s been around.

“Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: it’s going to be so bad your wedding is cancelled. But I’m getting married tomorrow. No, we have to fast now, we ain’t got time for that. Sister, shut up; brother, shut the hell up; this is going to be a major fast.

And it tells you why: “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” They are going to be torturing us; that’s why we are going to be praying and fasting, spare thy people, O Lord, because they are going to be killing the Israelites. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?” Didn’t we just read that in Wisdom of Solomon 2, where they mock us? Where is their God? I thought you said you were the people of God; where’s your God now?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land”: there is going to be something going on in the Middle East. “And pity his people”: because we are going to be in this part of the land over here. “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen.”

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”: something is going to pop off, and he said, I got to remove that army off of y’all. “And will drive him into a land barren and desolate”: that’s the land of Israel over there. “With his face toward the east sea”, the Dead Sea, “and his hinder part toward the utmost sea”, the Mediterranean Sea. “And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up”: the Lord is going to destroy them right there.

What took about two minutes to read is years, and none of it has popped off yet, because we have to grow to a certain point of spiritual understanding, every man and every woman. Your wife got to be strong: if something happens to you, she can’t fall apart, give up the Lord, have all the kids give up the Lord and go worshiping the white man. You get the lake of fire after that.

sense.text:
This is for the people that love us and are not going to turn their back on us. They are going to be rewarded for holding us down. When the ADL and the Southern Poverty Law Center are trying to shame us, they’re going to say, these are the men of the Lord, and go out of their way to help them.

“The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.” When Paul went to prison, people were ashamed of him. But this man said, this is a man of God; they locked him up for doing the Lord’s work. He was not ashamed to back him.
“But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.” That is dangerous, to be out looking for where Paul is at. He sought him out diligently anyway.

“The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day”: in that day, when judgment comes, his house is spared. Why? Because he cared. So the people that hold us down when we are going through the trials, the ones who say, if something happens to him, bring his whole family here, tell his wife she don’t have to worry, we’re going to cover everything, they will find mercy in that day.

“And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou knowest very well.” Y’all think the Most High is not watching. Some of you are here because the Most High knows that you care. The other ones that are moving fake, get out of here.

Isaiah 13 is called for because it talks about when the Assyrian comes into our land, as we read in Micah 5. “The burden of Babylon”: this Babylon here is not the Babylon of Nebuchadnezzar. This Babylon is Babylon the Great, America.

“Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”: the banner is the Holy Bible, and we must lift it up. This banner is the same thing Isaiah 11 talks about. The high mountain is Babylon the Great, America.

“Exalt the voice unto them”: don’t speak soft. Speak with authority and speak loud, like Christ did; his voice was as the sound of many waters. People get this soft, weak Jesus from the TV. “Shake the hand”: when you shake the hand, you are reproving them with God’s laws.

“That they may go into the gates of the nobles.” Why are we going to shake there, what is going to happen? This is when the dragon is going to use that to come against us. During the time of Christ, the Pharisees and scribes went to Pilate and Herod. These churches that hate this truth are going to do the same thing: they are going to go to their governors, they are going to go to the ADL and the SPLC, against the sons and daughters of God.

“I have commanded my sanctified ones”: the sanctified ones are you teachers. He commands us. The sanctified ones are the ones who are going to be shaking the hand and exalting the voice. The land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt, as Isaiah 19 said, because we are going to be prophesying what this Bible says is going to happen, and it is going to come to pass.

“I have also called my mighty ones for mine anger”: the mighty ones for his anger are the angels. Whatever we go through in this Bible, the angels are going to make sure it comes to pass.
“They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, even the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.” The weapons of his indignation are the missiles.

precepts.why: Who are the sanctified ones? “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.” So we are the sanctified ones, sanctified through Christ, and he commands us to lift up the banner, exalt the voice and shake the hand.

The mighty ones are the angels: “And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

So the sanctified ones are shaking the hand and exalting the voice, and the mighty ones called for his anger are his mighty angels, who come with Christ in flaming fire to take vengeance and make sure everything we read in this Bible comes to pass.

sense.text:
This is a warning for the teachers. Y’all say you want to lift up the banner, exalt the voice, shake the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles. Are you sure about that? Christ says “Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves”: he is sending us forth as sheep in the midst of wolves.

“Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.” When it comes to operating in this world we got to use wisdom in our comings and goings, and use the Bible to our advantage. Harmless as doves means don’t break God’s commandments.

“But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues”. That’s the ADL, the SPLC, Canary Mission, and the other groups out there working with the FBI.
“And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake”: they’ll say we’re disturbing the peace. It is “for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.”

Christ was warning us: when they deliver you up, don’t worry about what to say, “for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak.” The spirit is going to come on you. “For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you”: the spirit of our Father is going to speak.

Some of y’all are close with your family, and some of your brothers don’t believe. I’m talking about your blood brothers. Christ prophesied “the brother shall deliver up the brother to death”; that’s what we read in Wisdom of Solomon too. Some of your fathers are going to deliver up the children. And “the children shall rise up against their parents”: some of your kids are going to be no damn good, you see signs already, and they’re going to rise up against you “and cause them to be put to death.” Some of y’all think this could never happen, not in America. You watch and see.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”: we’re going to be hated of everybody, enemy number one. “But he that endureth to the end shall be saved”: if we endure to the end, until death, we’re going to be saved. Don’t worry about it.

“When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another”: if you’re able, leave from one city and run to the next. That’s why you don’t use your money frivolously. Whatever you got, think ahead. Not what if, but when.

“Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come” means we won’t reach all the Israelites on the planet by the time Christ returns.

“The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.” Christ is our Master; we are not above the Lord Christ. “It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord.”

“If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub”, meaning Lord of the Flies, wicked as hell, “how much more shall they call them of his household?” That’s why they call us names. I don’t get shocked, I don’t get amazed. Call us all kind of names, I don’t give a damn, that ain’t hurting me. Christ said don’t worry about the name calling: they’re going to call you names because they called Christ names too.

“Fear them not therefore”: Christ said don’t worry about them, don’t be scared. “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known”: everything that’s been hidden, we’re going to bring it out.

“What I tell you in darkness” means dark parables. “That speak ye in light”: explain it simple, crystal clear, in the open. What you hear in the ear in secret and in parables, “that preach ye upon the housetops”: make it plain for the nations to hear.

“And fear not them which kill the body”. He’s letting you know that based on what you teach, shaking the hand, you’re going to get killed. Don’t worry about them killing your body, because what you preach and teach will get you killed. To be a revolutionary in God’s army, some of us are going to have to die. Blood will have to be shed.

Martin and Malcolm didn’t understand the truth, but they understood that point. Fred Hampton understood that point too. Some of us are in the truth and still confused about why we got to die. The only thing that’s going to die is this body; your spirit, the real you, is still walking and talking with the Lord.

They are “not able to kill the soul”. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”: in hell, coming in the lake of fire. That’s who we got to fear.

“Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.” “The very hairs of your head are all numbered.” Christ said a sparrow won’t die unless the Father allows it to die, but don’t worry, “ye are of more value than many sparrows.” That’s how important we are.

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men”: this is in the face of death. He’s not talking about on your job; he’s talking about in fear of death, and it goes back to verse 28. It’s talking about torture. “Him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” This is what we read in Wisdom of Solomon chapter 2. Y’all got to connect the dots, put the posts together.

“But whosoever shall deny me before men”: Israelite, stop, don’t do that to me, don’t take my home, don’t take my house, don’t take my kids, I never believed that, Christ, stop. That’s what some of y’all are going to do. And Christ says “him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

precepts.why:
This is the precept for wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, to give you understanding. Paul says “I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.”

Wise unto that which is good: that’s God’s laws. Simple concerning evil is harmless as a dove, and evil means breaking God’s law. So the teacher sent out as a sheep among wolves stays wise in God’s laws and does not break them.

Christ spoke the parable: “Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.” “So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.” We see the kingdom of God is at hand now by the fact that brothers and sisters are waking up. “This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled”: this generation is back.

“Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.” Heaven and earth means the ruling powers on this heaven and this earth; they’re going to pass away, but Christ’s words never will.

“Take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting”. Surfeiting means excess: you’re doing too much, my man, going too much into sin, along with “drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.” If you are in the midst of adultery, child molestation, whatever your ups and downs and pitfalls, the day of the Lord is going to come on you unawares because you ain’t watching. “For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.”

“Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.” We all want to be accounted worthy to escape all these things, enduring to the end until the Son of man comes.

sense.text:
We went through all of that, the burden of Babylon, the warning to the teachers and the parable of the fig tree, to explain this verse. “And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof” means we are going to use the word of God as our sword, and we are going to teach and preach and shake kingdoms.

“Thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian”: the he is Christ. Why does he deliver us? Because the Assyrian is going to come against us, “when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.” They are going to come into our land and tread on our borders. He delivers us from the Assyrian, from the torture, the tribulation. That’s what it’s talking about, and it almost gets skipped over.

From verse 6 to verse 7 it doesn’t mention the wilderness. It mentions us being delivered, but it’s written so short we skip right by it. We’re delivered, we’re taken, caught up in the clouds, taken to the wilderness, as in Ezekiel 20.

Then “the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the Lord, as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men”: we ain’t going to wait for man nor the sons of men.

“The remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest”: we are going to be like lions among the beasts. “As a young lion among the flocks of sheep”: what can sheep do to a young lion? Nothing. They’re just food.

“Who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces”: that’s the threshing we read in Micah 4:13 about arise and thresh, repeated right here. “And none can deliver”: nobody is going to be able to deliver the nations from our hands. This proves the Lord is going to give us power, because in order for us to do that we need power.

“Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off”: we are going to cut off all our enemies. There’s going to be war on the armies of the heathen nations, all out war.

“I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee”: all the armies of the world that are in the midst of us, Christ said I’m going to cut them off. “And I will destroy thy chariots”: the chariots of the nations.
“And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds”. That’s the same thing Malachi 1:4 says about Esau, Edom.

“And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers”. God is letting us know they deal with witchcraft. We’ve been thinking these are some upstanding people; God says no, they deal with sorcery. They literally deal with witchcraft, sorcery, wizardry, necromancy.

“Thy graven images also will I cut off”: all the graven images here in America are going to be destroyed. “And thy standing images out of the midst of thee”: that’s the Statue of Liberty, the Washington Monument, the obelisks, all these monuments they got, Mount Rushmore. It’s all going. “And thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands.”
“And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee”: he will pluck up their churches out of the midst of them. And Christ said “so will I destroy thy cities.”

“And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen”: that heathen is the real heathen. “Such as they have not heard”: Christ said this destruction is going to be so bad, it’s like nothing you’ve ever heard before.

precepts.why:
An example of what Rome did, of the Assyrian treading within our borders. Paul says “ye had compassion of me in my bonds”: you had compassion on me when I was arrested. “And took joyfully the spoiling of your goods”: when they robbed their goods, “knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

They took the substance of these brothers and sisters: their homes, their houses, their cattle, whatever they owned, they took from the believers. That’s what happened to the Hebrews that followed Christ, and Paul said they rejoiced. That’s another level of faith we’ve got to get to, because some of you are very attached: that’s my home, that’s my house. What will you do for your home and your house? Will you give up this truth, the understanding of this truth, before the enemies of God?

Some brothers lose their job and the sister leaves him. That’s why it’s important, brothers, that your woman is loyal. The woman you marry must fear God and love God, and the same hope you have she must have too, because once you lose everything she’s going to be right there supporting you. So I behoove you brothers, make sure your woman understands these things. Otherwise, when things get bad, she’s gone; she will turn on you.

The Lord has to give us power. “In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem”: that’s what we read in Micah 5, “thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian”.

“And he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”: he that is feeble among us shall be as David, and David was one of the mightiest men on the planet. “And the house of David shall be as God”: the 144 are going to be as God on this planet earth, “as the angel of the Lord”. There’s some power right there. That’s what I’m talking about: the Lord has got to give us that power.

“Fear not, thou worm Jacob”: the Lord is telling us this because we ain’t nothing. Women look at us like y’all ain’t nothing. Right now we are worms. But read on: “and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.” God is going to help us.

What is he going to do? “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth”. That’s the same thing we read in Micah 4:13, arise and thresh, meaning beat the hell out of the nations. He’s going to cut us loose. “Thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small”: we are going to thresh the nations and beat them small, “and shalt make the hills as chaff.”

“Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away”: we’re going to fan the nations and the wind is going to carry them, because we’re going to burn them up. “And the whirlwind shall scatter them”: that’s the chariots. “And thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, and shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel”: we’re going to praise the Lord and glory in the Holy One of Israel. This is the young lion tearing in pieces in Micah 5:8.

There’s going to be war on the armies of the heathen nations. “Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that’s the judgment of God, and that’s why he’s going to give us power. Every nation that put their dirty bloody hands on us is going to be devoured, every last one of them.

“And all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: all our enemies, every one of them, man and woman. That’s what the Bible says, that’s what the Son of God says, that’s what God says.

“And they that spoil thee shall be a spoil”: every nation that robbed us, we’re going to rob them. “And all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey”: God is going to give every nation that preyed upon us for a prey. That’s why he called us that young lion. We’re going to hunt them down and take them by power and fire.

This says the same thing about Esau, Edom. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: they’re always playing victim. “But we will return and build the desolate places”: they said we will return, during the Renaissance, and build cities after cities worldwide.

“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”: the white man shall build city after city, but Christ will throw down. That’s the same thing as Micah 5:11, cutting off the cities and throwing down the strong holds.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” You know what that’s saying? The white man is the devil. The Bible speaks it; that’s the border of wickedness. Every one of them, all of them, man, woman, boy, girl. Get mad if you want. And for how long? “For ever.” We can’t change that.

They literally deal with witchcraft, sorcery, wizardry, necromancy. “But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood”: the citizens in this country are going to be put to death when war comes. “They shall come upon thee in their perfection”: the nations shall come upon them in their perfection, “for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.”

Verse one tells you this is spoken to the virgin daughter of Babylon. Now God tells Babylon, the white man: “Stand now with thine enchantments”, their witchcraft, “and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth”. They’ve always dealt in witchcraft. That’s how they got world domination, through operating with Satan. “If so be thou shalt be able to profit, if so be thou mayest prevail.”

That’s where their scientists are learning from, evil spirits.

“Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot”: America is the well favoured harlot. She is the woman of Revelation 17 that sat on the dragon with seven heads. That’s her. “The mistress of witchcrafts”: God calls America the mistress of witchcrafts.

“That selleth nations through her whoredoms”: if you didn’t think it was America, it says she sells nations. That’s this place here, and the nations they sold were Judah and Israel. They sold us into slavery. “And families through her witchcrafts”: our families. These are the witchcrafts God cuts off out of her hand in Micah 5:12.
